evidence.source_sentence: The lack of toughness and heat resistance of polyvinyl chloride (PVC) limit its application in construction, transportation, packaging, and medical treatment.
In this work, the core–shell structure polybutadiene grafted styrene and acrylonitrile copolymer (PB-g-SAN), named (ABS), was utilized to toughen PVC.
The heat-resistant modifier styrene-N-phenylmaleimide-acrylonitrile terpolymer (SMIA) synthesized by bulk polymerization was added to PVC/ABS to improve the heat resistance of the composite.

The Vicat softening temperature of the ternary functional composite (PVC/ABS/SMIA, 72:8:20) raised by $2 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C } ,$, and the initial decomposition temperature increased by $1 9 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C } .$.

Polyvinyl chloride (PVC) resin has attracted wide attention in construction, transportation, packaging, and medical applications because of its low cost, corrosion resistance, and flame retardancy [1–3].

The polybutadiene grafted styrene and acrylonitrile copolymer (PB-g-SAN), named (ABS), is a class of core–shell graft copolymer modifiers synthesized by emulsion polymerization, with polybutadiene (PBL) rubber as the core and polystyrene-co-acrylonitrile as the shell [12].

Blending with components possessing high glass transition temperature is a selectable method to elevate the heat resistance of PVC [17].
reported an α-MSAN, PVC, and ABS ternary composite material.
fabricated a-methylstyrene/NPMI acrylonitrile random copolymer, MSAMI, which dramatically improves the heat resistance of ABS [22].
prepared monodisperse poly(N-phenylmaleimide)-acrylonitrile–styrene copolymers through the method of seeded microemulsion polym erization.

As displayed in Figure 2, only one single Tg appeared at 123.5°C in the DSC curves of the terpolymer SMIA, and the results agree with the empirical formula proposed by Fox et al. [20] which indicated that the structure of copolymer SMIA is relatively homogeneous.

The field emission SEM was used to explore the micromorphology of the impact fracture surface. As displayed in Figure  4a, the impact section of the composite material presents relatively flat with the addition of 6 phr ABS. The impact section of the PVC/ABS composite material contains well-distributed voids when the ABS is increased to 10 phr (Figure 4c). Some tree-root-like yielding fibers appear, which is a typical characteristic of toughness fracture. The fracture surface is not uniform at 12 phr (Figure 4d). Both the matrix yielding caused by the obvious plastic deformation and a number of voids, and some of the more flat and smooth planes appear the characteristics of brittle fracture.

To deeply understand the impact performance of PVC/ABS/ SMIA composites, SEM images were acquired. As shown in Figure $^ { 6 , }$the boundary between the two phases was not found, and no obvious phase separation occurred. The gradual decrease in the number of yielding fibers on the surface can be observed when the SMIA content is increased from 0 to 10 phr. As the SMIA content further increases, the degree of slatting increases, the surface becomes relatively smooth, and the number of micropores gradually decreases.
